articles.whyItMatters: System administrators should review this list to find and apply patches affecting their distributions.

articles.title: Debian-Based and systemd-Free antiX Linux 26.1 Released
articles.brief: antiX Linux 26.1 is now available for download, based on Debian 13 "Trixie" and built without systemd/libsystemd0 or elogind/libelogind0.
articles.whyItMatters: Users seeking a Debian-based distribution without systemd or elogind may find this release relevant.

articles.title: antiX Linux 26.1 released, based on Debian 13 and free of systemd
articles.author: Marcus Nestor
articles.brief: antiX Linux 26.1 is available for download, based on Debian 13 "Trixie" and shipping without systemd/libsystemd0 or elogind/libelogind0. The release also includes updated kernels.
articles.whyItMatters: Users seeking a Debian-based distribution without systemd can now upgrade to a release tracking Debian 13.

articles.title: OpenSSL 4.0.3 Security Patch Release Available
articles.brief: OpenSSL 4.0.3 is out with bug fixes and mitigations for various security vulnerabilities in the open-source TLS/SSL and crypto library. Users are advised to update.
articles.whyItMatters: Anyone running or shipping OpenSSL-based software should update to address the disclosed vulnerabilities.

articles.title: OpenSSL 4.0.3 Security Patch Release Available
articles.author: Marcus Nestor
articles.brief: OpenSSL 4.0.3 is now available for download, bringing bug fixes and mitigations for various security vulnerabilities in the open-source TLS/SSL and crypto library.
articles.whyItMatters: Anyone running OpenSSL-based services should update to address the security vulnerabilities.

articles.title: hw-monitor 0.6 Released With Per-Process GPU Usage & Memory Reporting
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: hw-monitor 0.6, a Linux system monitoring tool, adds per-process GPU usage and memory reporting on capable DRM drivers. The release also includes a startup-applications tab, sensors UI improvements, and bug fixes, followed by a 0.6.1 fix-up release.
keyPoints: Per-process GPU usage and memory columns with AMDGPU, Intel i915/Xe, and Nouveau drivers
New tab listing startup applications from XDG autostart entries
Sensors UI and theme improvements; 0.6.1 adds more fixes
articles.whyItMatters: Linux users tracking GPU workloads per application get a modern monitoring option with driver-level reporting.

articles.title: Firefox 157 ships Nova redesign as default, with an opt-out
articles.author: Sourav Rudra
articles.brief: Mozilla's Nova redesign, leaked in March, is now the default look in Firefox 157, bringing rounder tabs and address bar, refreshed settings cards, and improved Tab Groups. The final design drops the leaked mockups' floating island and rounded web content container. Users can revert via about:config.
keyPoints: Rounder tabs, address bar, and slimmer toolbar; settings panels now sit in rounded cards
Tab Groups feel more complete; compact mode returns under Window density settings
Disable Nova via browser.nova.enabled in about:config
articles.whyItMatters: Firefox users on Linux will receive the redesign through routine distro updates, and those who dislike it can revert.

articles.title: NOCL Making Progress As Mesa Gallium/OpenCL Atop NVIDIA CUDA
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Karol Herbst presented at XDC 2026 on NOCL, a compute-only Mesa Gallium driver that runs OpenCL via Rusticl atop NVIDIA's proprietary CUDA driver API using PTX. The merge request is still pending, but the driver already supports more OpenCL extensions than NVIDIA's own OpenCL driver.
keyPoints: NOCL is a compute-only Gallium driver pairing Rusticl with NVIDIA's CUDA driver API and PTX
Supports more OpenCL extensions than NVIDIA's proprietary OpenCL driver
PTX-to-NIR work will matter for features like DLSS with the NVK driver
articles.whyItMatters: Developers and users on NVIDIA's proprietary Linux driver gain an open-source OpenCL option, and the PTX work feeds into NVK.

articles.title: How to Upgrade Ubuntu 24.04 LTS to Ubuntu 26.04 LTS
articles.brief: 9to5Linux has published a step-by-step tutorial with screenshots showing how to upgrade Ubuntu 24.04 LTS (Noble Numbat) installations to Ubuntu 26.04 LTS (Resolute Raccoon). The upgrade path is now available to users.
articles.whyItMatters: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS users who want the newer 26.04 LTS release can follow this guide to perform the upgrade.

articles.title: You Can Now Upgrade Ubuntu 24.04 LTS to Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, Here's How
articles.author: Marcus Nestor
articles.brief: 9to5Linux has published a step-by-step tutorial, with screenshots, showing how to upgrade Ubuntu 24.04 LTS (Noble Numbat) installations to Ubuntu 26.04 LTS (Resolute Raccoon).
articles.whyItMatters: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS users considering a move to the 26.04 LTS release can follow this guide.

articles.title: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS Users Can Now Upgrade to Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: Canonical has enabled the LTS-to-LTS upgrade path from Ubuntu 24.04 to Ubuntu 26.04.1 "Resolute Raccoon." Desktop users get a phased Update Manager notification; server users can run do-release-upgrade manually. The release brings kernel 7.0, GNOME 50, and a Wayland-only desktop.
keyPoints: Upgrade via Update Manager rollout or sudo do-release-upgrade
Ships Linux kernel 7.0 and GNOME 50 with Wayland-only session
New default apps: Ptyxis, Loupe, Papers, Resources, Showtime
articles.whyItMatters: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS users who skipped interim releases can now upgrade directly to the latest LTS, supported until May 2031, without a clean install.

articles.title: Mesa 26.3 Enables Intel's Jay Shader Compiler by Default on Xe2/Xe3
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Mesa 26.3 now enables Jay, a new Intel GPU shader compiler led by Alyssa Rosenzweig, by default on Xe2 and Xe3 platforms including Battlemage, Lunar Lake, and Panther Lake. Jay is about 10% faster than the BRW compiler overall and compiles Fossil 55% faster than BRW, 66% faster than the Windows driver.
keyPoints: Jay enabled by default for Xe2/Xe3: Battlemage, Lunar Lake, Panther Lake
About 10% faster than existing BRW compiler
Fossil compile times 55% faster than BRW, 66% faster than Windows driver
articles.whyItMatters: Intel Linux graphics users get faster shader compilation and modest performance gains out of the box in Mesa 26.3.

articles.title: antiX 26.1 Released as a Debian 13-Based, systemd-Free Linux
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: antiX 26.1 is out, based on Debian 13 "Trixie," as a bug-fix update to the lightweight, systemd-free distribution. It offers five init systems with runit as default, two kernel options, and Full and Core images for both 64-bit and 32-bit hardware.
keyPoints: Five init choices (runit, SysVinit, dinit, s6-rc, s6-66); no systemd, elogind, Snap, or Flatpak
Kernels: customized 5.10.256, plus 6.6.139 in the 64-bit Full edition
Full (~2 GB) and Core (~660 MB) images, both with official 32-bit support
articles.whyItMatters: Users who want a lightweight, systemd-free Debian-based distro, especially on older 32-bit hardware, get an updated option.

articles.title: BPF-Based MIPI DSI Display Panel Drivers Proposed for Linux
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Maxime Ripard posted a patch series proposing BPF-based MIPI DSI panel drivers, following the HID-BPF model. The approach lets panel drivers ship separately from the kernel, addressing OEMs' need for quick panel swaps and distros' slow kernel update cycles. It works with Raspberry Pi Touch Display 2 panels.
keyPoints: MIPI DSI panels typically need a custom, poorly documented init driver each
BPF programs ship separately from the kernel with their own lifecycle
Userspace component started by udev would load the right BPF program
articles.whyItMatters: Kernel and distro developers should care because this could decouple panel support from slow kernel release cycles.

articles.title: D7VK 2.3 Released, Project Declared Mature and Enters Maintenance Mode
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: D7VK, a Vulkan-based implementation of Direct3D 7/6/5/3 for Linux and Wine/Steam Play, released version 2.3 with a possibly final performance optimization around shadow surface memory placement. The developer now considers the project mature and is moving it into maintenance mode with no major new features planned.
keyPoints: Imperial Age performance rose from 80 to 137 FPS, up from 62 FPS on D7VK 2.0
Re-based against DXVK 3.1.1 with improved Vulkan side checks and fixes
Project enters maintenance mode; no major new features expected
articles.whyItMatters: Linux gamers running older Direct3D titles via Wine or Steam Play get a faster, now stable translation layer.

articles.title: Large Folios Able To Deliver Big Performance Gains For FUSE With Linux 7.4
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: A patch enabling large folios for FUSE has landed in the FUSE for-next branch and is expected to be merged for Linux 7.4. Large folios group contiguous physical pages into one folio for lower overhead, and will be enabled when not under memory pressure.
keyPoints: Large folios patch queued in FUSE for-next branch, expected in Linux 7.4
Large folios group contiguous pages into one folio for lower overhead
Benchmarks show strong gains on TMPFS and XFS/NVMe cold I/O with passthrough_hp
articles.whyItMatters: Users of FUSE-based filesystems in user-space should care, as Linux 7.4 may bring significant I/O performance improvements.

articles.title: Igalia Improving The Firefox Experience For Valve's Steam Deck
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Igalia, working with Valve, presented at XDC 2026 on improving Firefox on the Steam Deck by moving it to native Wayland under the Gamescope compositor, replacing the limited X11 path. Fixes cover gamepad input, fullscreen, touch scrolling, notifications, and HDR video.
keyPoints: Firefox on Steam Deck is transitioning to native Wayland via Gamescope's wl_compositor protocol
Fixes target gamepad input, fullscreen handling, touch-scroll stutter, notifications, and HDR video
Ongoing work: upstreaming Gamescope patches, replacing udev with inputfd, session management
articles.whyItMatters: Steam Deck owners and Wayland/Gamescope developers should care, as this upstreams fixes for one of Linux gaming's most visible browser experiences.

articles.title: AMD Ryzen Zen 6 CPU Power Values Being Further Tuned For Linux
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: AMD engineers posted a new patch refining power and performance characteristics for upcoming Zen 6 Ryzen client CPUs in the AMD P-State Linux driver. It adjusts Energy Performance Preference (EPP) values for the performance and new low-power core types, continuing pre-launch tuning that suggests Linux 7.4 as an…
keyPoints: Patch tunes EPP values for Zen 6 performance and low-power cores
Performance core power EPP rises from 64 to 115; low-power values shift 51 to 64 and 115 to 64
Linux 7.4 eyed as initial sweet spot for next-gen Ryzen support
articles.whyItMatters: Linux users planning to run future Zen 6 Ryzen systems should track these kernel patches for proper power/performance behavior.

articles.title: KDE Plasma 6.8 Beta 2 Polishes UI Ahead of October 14 Release
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: KDE's weekly update details the second Plasma 6.8 beta with UI refinements and bug fixes before the October 14 final release. Early Plasma 6.9 changes are also landing, and a KDE documentary premieres on the project's 30th anniversary the same day.
keyPoints: Plasma 6.8 improves tray click feedback, lock screen layout switching, and BLE pairing.
Fixes include clipboard crash, KRunner journal flooding, and wetter.com nighttime temperatures.
Plasma 6.9, due February 2027, adds flexible currency conversion in KRunner.
articles.whyItMatters: Plasma users and KDE followers get a preview of near-term desktop fixes and the project's anniversary plans.

articles.title: GoZen 0.14 Video Editor Enters Beta, Built With Godot and FFmpeg
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: GoZen, a minimalist open-source video editor built with Godot and FFmpeg, has released version 0.14, its first beta. It adds effects like Glow, Shake, and Glitch plus many reliability fixes, with future betas focusing on polish ahead of 1.0.
keyPoints: First beta of minimalist Godot-based video editor, primarily for Linux
New effects: Glow, Scroll, Shear, Shake, Glitch; unified audio/video timeline
Fixes crashes, timeline and waveform bugs; Steam release planned at 1.0
articles.whyItMatters: Linux content creators seeking a lightweight, open-source video editor gain a new option now stable enough for beta testing.

articles.title: gThumb 4.0 released with GTK4/libadwaita rewrite
articles.author: Joey Sneddon
articles.brief: gThumb 4.0 is out as a stable release, completing the photo manager's GTK4 and libadwaita rewrite with a refreshed interface. It adds a censor tool, animated WebP/PNG support, JPEG XL saving, and touchpad gestures, while dropping web albums, contact sheets, and the find-duplicates tool.
keyPoints: Full GTK4/libadwaita port with reworked UI and improved backend performance
New censor tool, JPEG XL saving, animated WebP/PNG, gesture and mouse-button navigation
Removed: web albums, contact sheet, find duplicates; source and PPA available, Flathub not yet updated
articles.whyItMatters: GNOME users who manage photo collections get a modernized gThumb, though Ubuntu repos still ship the old GTK3 version.

articles.title: "Shiva" Being Developed For Mesa Vulkan Drivers, Akin To Gallium3D
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Collabora's Faith Ekstrand presented Shiva at XDC 2026, a proposed Mesa framework that would give Vulkan drivers a shared abstraction layer like Gallium3D does for OpenGL. It aims to reduce fragmentation as Vulkan grows more complex, with roughly two years before users see results.
keyPoints: Drivers would target the Shiva API instead of Vulkan directly, easing shared code and abstractions
Initial work targets Nouveau and Arm Mali Panfrost drivers, with Rust drivers in mind
Estimated two years before the work benefits users
articles.whyItMatters: Mesa and Vulkan driver developers should care because this could reshape how Linux GPU drivers are built and shared.

articles.title: Guessing the Ubuntu 27.04 codename: it will be a "T" adjective plus animal
articles.author: Joey Sneddon
articles.brief: An OMG! Ubuntu writer speculates on the codename for Ubuntu 27.04, due April 2027, which by tradition pairs a T adjective with a T animal. The piece analyzes patterns from past codenames and lists candidate T animals, landing on a personal guess of "Thrifty Tapir."
keyPoints: Ubuntu 27.04 will be a T.T. codename following Stonking Stingray (26.10)
37.8% of past adjectives end in -y; most animals have two syllables
Author's guess: Thrifty Tapir
articles.whyItMatters: Light reading for Ubuntu fans who enjoy the distro's codename traditions.

articles.title: Emmabuntüs Debian Edition 1.03 Adds New Accessibility Features, Debian 13.7 Base
articles.brief: Emmabuntüs Debian Edition 1.03 is now available for download. It is based on Debian GNU/Linux 13.7 "Trixie" and introduces new accessibility features.

articles.title: Emmabuntüs Debian Edition 1.03 Adds Accessibility Features, Debian 13.7 Base
articles.author: Marcus Nestor
articles.brief: Emmabuntüs Debian Edition 6 1.03 is now available, rebased on Debian GNU/Linux 13.7 "Trixie" and introducing new accessibility features. Only a teaser was available, so further details are unknown.
articles.whyItMatters: Users of this refurbishing-focused distro may want the updated Debian base and accessibility improvements.

articles.title: Mozilla Firefox 158 Enters Public Beta Testing with Better PDF Handling on Linux
articles.brief: Firefox 158 is now available for public beta testing. The teaser mentions better PDF handling on Linux, New Tab improvements, and other changes, but no further details were available.
articles.whyItMatters: Linux users who test Firefox betas may want to try the improved PDF handling early.

articles.title: Firefox 158 Enters Public Beta with Better PDF Handling on Linux
articles.author: Marcus Nestor
articles.brief: Mozilla has opened public beta testing for Firefox 158. The teaser mentions improved PDF handling, New Tab improvements, and other changes, with only partial details available.
articles.whyItMatters: Firefox users and testers on Linux can preview upcoming browser improvements ahead of the stable release.

articles.title: KDE Plasma 6.8 Gives the Oxygen Theme More Modern Touches
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: KDE's classic Oxygen theme gets a modernization pass in Plasma 6.8, due October 14. Key changes include full accent-color support, a refreshed cursor set from original designer Nuno Pinheiro, fractional-scaling fixes, and an option to disable the title bar gradient.
keyPoints: Oxygen and Air window glows now follow the system accent color
Cursor theme gains more sizes and a new busy animation
Fractional scaling fixes for radio buttons, sliders, and title bars
articles.whyItMatters: KDE users and distro maintainers who ship or prefer the Oxygen theme should know it now handles accent colors and fractional scaling properly.

articles.title: qBittorrent 5.2.4 Open-Source BitTorrent Client Released with WebUI Improvements
articles.brief: qBittorrent 5.2.4 is now available for download, shipping various bug fixes and improvements focused mainly on the web-based user interface.
articles.whyItMatters: qBittorrent users, especially those using the WebUI for remote management, may want to update for the fixes.

articles.title: qBittorrent 5.2.4 Released with WebUI Improvements
articles.author: Marcus Nestor
articles.brief: qBittorrent 5.2.4, an open-source BitTorrent client, is now available for download. The update brings bug fixes and improvements, mainly to the web-based user interface.

articles.title: NVIDIA Building Open-Source Display Config Server for Linux Display Walls
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: NVIDIA engineer Austin Shafer presented at XDC 2026 a new Display Config Server aimed at complex display walls, which today often run Windows or X.Org with NVIDIA Mosaic. It builds on Vulkan direct-to-display (VK_KHR_display), owning displays and leasing them to Vulkan clients so apps avoid handling calibration and…
keyPoints: Targets video walls in TV production and theaters, mostly Windows-based today
Server owns displays and leases them to Vulkan clients for centralized configuration
Work underway to run it nested with a Wayland compositor
articles.whyItMatters: Developers and integrators building Linux-based video walls get a simpler path off X.Org and Windows toward Wayland/Vulkan.

articles.title: SIMDjson 5.0 Released: Still Making JSON Parsing Even Faster
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: SIMDjson 5.0 is out, promoting static reflection support to an officially supported feature and improving big integer handling, along with smaller features and performance optimizations. Independent Phoronix benchmarks against 4.6.4 show decent speed gains.
keyPoints: Static reflection support is now an officially supported feature
Better handling of big integer numbers
Benchmarks show speed gains over SIMDjson 4.6.4
articles.whyItMatters: Developers parsing large volumes of JSON should care, since SIMDjson keeps raising parsing throughput with each release.

articles.title: Git 2.56 Adds New Options for Cleaning Up Branches and Resolving Conflicts
articles.brief: Git 2.56 is now available for download with new features, options, and performance improvements, including options for cleaning up branches and resolving conflicts.

articles.title: Git 2.56 Adds New Options for Cleaning Up Branches and Resolving Conflicts
articles.author: Marcus Nestor
articles.brief: Git 2.56 is now available for download with new features, new options for branch cleanup and conflict resolution, and performance improvements.
articles.whyItMatters: Git users interested in new branch-management and conflict-resolution options will want to see the release details.

articles.title: Git 2.56 Released With Safer Conflict Resolution and Performance Gains
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: Git 2.56 adds a safer way to stage conflict resolutions, easier branch cleanup, and new history-editing features. It also delivers notable performance gains on very large repositories, per GitHub, plus improved repacking and bisect behavior.
keyPoints: git add --resolved stages conflict fixes and checks for leftover conflict markers
New git branch --delete-merged and expanded git refs command
Large-repo performance gains in merge-base calculations and path-walk repacking
articles.whyItMatters: Developers, especially those maintaining large repositories, gain safer conflict workflows and faster Git operations.

articles.title: Git v2.56.0 released
articles.author: jake
articles.brief: Git 2.56.0 is out with 748 non-merge commits from 104 contributors, 39 of them new. Highlights include new `git refs` subcommands, an experimental `git history drop` subcommand, a `git add --resolved` option, and numerous performance and refactoring improvements.
keyPoints: New `git refs` create, delete, update, and rename subcommands
`git add --resolved` stages conflict-resolved paths only
Experimental `git history drop` removes a commit and replays descendants
articles.whyItMatters: Anyone using Git daily will benefit from the new workflow commands and performance fixes; packagers should note the new release.

articles.title: Fedora 45 to Offer Smoother Experience on Snapdragon X1 Laptops
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Fedora 45, due in October, will ship with improved Qualcomm Snapdragon X1 laptop support thanks to upstream kernel work and distribution-level fixes led by Hans de Goede, who moved from Red Hat to Qualcomm last year.
keyPoints: Snapdragon X1 support polished via mainline kernel work and Fedora-level enhancements
Fedora 45 ships Linux 7.2; X2 support lands in future kernels
A few hardware-specific workarounds may still be required
articles.whyItMatters: Users considering ARM-based Snapdragon X1 laptops now have a more viable Fedora option.

articles.title: Reducing undefined behavior in the C language
articles.author: corbet
articles.brief: At Kernel Recipes, biomedical engineering professor and longtime Linux user Martin Uecker talked about undefined behavior in C and whether the language can eventually be made memory-safe. He works on free software for controlling MRI scanners.
articles.whyItMatters: C programmers and kernel developers interested in memory safety will want to see the talk's arguments.

articles.title: Security updates for Monday
articles.author: jake
articles.brief: LWN's weekly roundup lists security updates from AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora, Mageia, Oracle, SUSE, and Ubuntu. Affected packages include kernel, firefox, chromium, libxml2, exim4, libvirt, and lxc, among many others.
keyPoints: AlmaLinux and Oracle issued kernel and libxml2 updates across multiple releases
Debian patched exim4, ghostscript, chromium, and php8.4 in stable
Ubuntu fixed libvirt, lxc, exim4, and freerdp3 across supported LTS releases
articles.whyItMatters: System administrators should review the list for packages they run and apply the relevant patches.

articles.title: Firefox 157 Now Available With Visual Refresh, WebRTC Hardware AV1 Decode
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Mozilla released Firefox 157, featuring the Nova UI, described as the browser's biggest visual refresh in years, updating chrome, sidebar, and menus. It also adds hardware AV1 decoding for WebRTC video calls on supported devices, HDR video fixes, and removes Amazon as a built-in search engine.
keyPoints: Nova UI modernizes browser chrome, sidebar, and menus
WebRTC now supports hardware AV1 decoding on supported devices
HDR video fixes; Amazon removed as built-in search engine
articles.whyItMatters: Firefox users and web developers should care about the visual overhaul and improved WebRTC video performance.

articles.title: Flatpak 1.18.4 Released With Fixes for Six Security Vulnerabilities
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: Flatpak 1.18.4 is a security update fixing six newly disclosed vulnerabilities in the Linux app sandboxing framework, plus related hardening. Fixes cover arbitrary file overwrite and deletion, OCI token exposure, desktop file filtering, and sandbox signal escapes.
keyPoints: CVE-2026-97024 and CVE-2026-97023: malicious apps could overwrite or delete arbitrary files with elevated privileges.
CVE-2026-97025/26: OCI auth tokens and temp repository directory permissions are now restricted.
CVE-2026-97027/29: stricter .desktop and D-Bus file filtering; fixes signal escape that could kill the desktop.
articles.whyItMatters: Linux users and distributions shipping Flatpak should update promptly to close sandbox-escape and privilege issues.

articles.title: Firefox 157 'Nova' Released With Biggest Visual Refresh in Years
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: Mozilla shipped Firefox 157, featuring Project Nova, a visual overhaul of the browser chrome, sidebar, and menus with a cleaner, rounded design. It also adds built-in light and dark themes, a compact mode, and hardware AV1 decoding for WebRTC calls.
keyPoints: Project Nova redesigns browser chrome, sidebar, and menus with updated design system
New built-in themes and compact mode for smaller screens
Hardware AV1 decoding now supported for WebRTC video calls
articles.whyItMatters: Firefox users on all platforms get a major UI refresh and better video call performance, rolling out via updates and distro repositories.

articles.title: Mozilla Firefox 157 Is Now Available with New Nova Design
articles.brief: Mozilla Firefox 157 is available for download with the new Nova design, HDR improvements, and better audio/video synchronization.
articles.whyItMatters: Firefox users and Linux desktop readers may care about the visual refresh and media playback improvements.

articles.title: postmarketOS rebrands to Nura
articles.author: Sourav Rudra
articles.brief: postmarketOS, the mobile Linux OS for reviving old smartphones, has been renamed Nura. The old descriptive name couldn't be trademarked and was often misstated; the new name references Sardinia's ancient Nuraghe stone towers, symbolizing longevity. Current release is v26.06.
keyPoints: Rename closed a year-long process with 300+ community name submissions
Trademark application filed for Nura, which was legally impossible with the old name
Project recommends Snapdragon 845 or 410/412 devices as entry points
articles.whyItMatters: Users of Linux phones and anyone reviving old smartphones should know the project's new identity and trademark status.

articles.title: Flatpak 1.18.4 Released With Important Security Fixes
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Flatpak 1.18.4 is out with several security fixes for the app sandboxing and distribution framework. Fixes cover privileged file overwrites and deletions by malicious apps, leaked OCI authentication tokens, and multiple denial-of-service vectors. A 1.19.2 development release with the same fixes is also available.
keyPoints: Blocks privileged overwrite or deletion of arbitrary files by malicious apps
Stops OCI repository authentication tokens from being visible to other users
Filters .desktop and D-Bus service files; blocks signals to host process groups
articles.whyItMatters: Linux users and distributors relying on Flatpak should update promptly, since the fixes close sandbox escapes and denial-of-service holes.

articles.title: Flatpak 1.18.4 Linux App Sandboxing Framework Fixes Security Issues
articles.brief: Flatpak 1.18.4, a maintenance release of the Linux app sandboxing and distribution framework, is now available. It delivers security fixes for the stable 1.18 series; the teaser does not detail which vulnerabilities are addressed.

articles.title: NVIDIA Vera SMT Performance Benchmarks: First Look
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Phoronix begins benchmarking a dual-socket NVIDIA Vera system with 176 Olympus cores and 352 threads, testing the impact of Vera's new Spatial Multithreading, which partitions core resources physically rather than time-slicing. Results are not included in this teaser.
keyPoints: Vera SMT gives two threads per core via physical resource partitioning, unlike AMD/Intel SMT
Tests compare SMT on vs off on a 176-core dual-socket Vera system
Power and frequency also monitored; more Vera articles coming
articles.whyItMatters: Readers interested in NVIDIA's new Vera ARM server CPUs get an early look at how its unusual SMT design performs.

articles.title: F-Droid 2.0 Android App Store Launches With New UI, Improved Search
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: F-Droid released version 2.0 of its official Android client, its biggest update in a decade, with a Kotlin/Jetpack Compose interface and overhauled discovery, search, and filtering. It drops Android 6 and Privileged Extension support, and the Nearby sharing feature is being rebuilt.
keyPoints: Redesigned UI in Kotlin and Jetpack Compose with Discover, Search, and My Apps sections
Search now covers descriptions, categories, and translations, with better CJK handling
Uses newer Android install APIs for smoother background installs and updates
articles.whyItMatters: Android users who rely on FOSS apps get a modernized store, but those on older devices or using the Privileged Extension must stay on legacy releases.

articles.title: AMD PerfOpt brings IOMMU bypass for AMD iGPUs in Linux 7.4
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Linux 7.4 will enable AMD PerfOpt by default, letting AMD integrated GPUs bypass the IOMMU when directly accessing system memory to cut overhead and boost performance. The feature applies to iGPUs only, can be disabled via the amdgpu.iommu_perfopt module parameter, and shows as "PerfOpt" in dmesg.
keyPoints: PerfOpt lets AMD iGPUs bypass IOMMU GPA->SPA translations, keeping IR/IW permission checks
Enabled by default for AMD iGPUs in Linux 7.4 via the IOMMU tree
Disable with amdgpu.iommu_perfopt parameter; not for discrete GPUs
articles.whyItMatters: Linux users with AMD integrated graphics, especially Ryzen AI Max systems, should see lower memory-access overhead and better iGPU performance.

articles.title: Firefox 157 released with Nova theme, its biggest visual refresh in years
articles.author: Joey Sneddon
articles.brief: Firefox 157 ships with the Nova theme enabled by default, bringing rounder tabs, menus, and address bars with pastel gradients across Windows, macOS, and opt-in Linux. It also restores an official compact mode, and Nova can be disabled via the browser.nova.enabled flag in about:config.
keyPoints: Nova theme is default; toned down from earlier Nightly 'floating islands' mockups
Compact mode returns officially, with an auto setting for small screens
Warning shown if SSLKEYLOGFILE key logging is enabled
articles.whyItMatters: Firefox users should know how the UI changes, how to revert Nova, and when the update reaches their Linux distribution.

articles.title: GhostBSD is Replacing MATE With a New Desktop Named After a Typo
articles.author: Sourav Rudra
articles.brief: GhostBSD lead Eric Turgeon is building Mocka, a from-scratch desktop environment meant to eventually replace MATE one component at a time. The first piece, Mocka Dock, is available as an alpha, with a menu, settings app, and website also in early development. Nothing changes for current users yet.
keyPoints: Mocka replaces MATE component by component until full feature parity
Mocka Dock alpha available now; menu and settings app in planning
New components stay MATE-compatible so users can mix and match
articles.whyItMatters: GhostBSD users and BSD desktop watchers should know the distribution's default desktop experience is being rebuilt from scratch.

articles.title: openSUSE Leap 16.1 RC Released With New Immutable Mode
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: openSUSE Leap 16.1 has entered release candidate testing alongside SUSE Linux Enterprise Server 16.1. Its headline feature is a new immutable mode with transactional updates and a read-only root filesystem, selectable in the installer. The RC also ships KDE Plasma 6.6, GNOME 48, and LXQt 2.4.
keyPoints: Immutable mode offers transactional updates with a read-only root filesystem
Immutable mode is intended to replace Leap Micro for container and VM hosts
RC includes KDE Plasma 6.6, GNOME 48, and LXQt 2.4
articles.whyItMatters: openSUSE users and admins running container or VM hosts should care, since immutable mode changes how Leap systems will be deployed and updated going forward.

articles.title: Linux 7.4 to introduce steal governor for virtualized workloads
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: IBM's steal governor driver, now queued in tip's sched/core branch, is expected for the Linux 7.4 merge window. It tracks vCPU steal time and dynamically adjusts preferred CPU masks so the scheduler avoids over-committed, contended CPUs, helping both POWER and x86_64 VMs.
keyPoints: Tracks steal time to avoid placing tasks on heavily contended CPUs
Benchmarks: Kernbench up to 14% faster, Hackbench up to 44%, Daytrader 1.53x
Best for preemption-sensitive workloads like databases; may slightly regress pure CPU tasks
articles.whyItMatters: Operators running over-committed VMs on high-core-count servers can expect better scheduler throughput for contention-sensitive workloads.

articles.title: Shotcut 26.9 Video Editor Released with UI Refresh and Audio Ducking
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Shotcut 26.9, the open-source non-linear video editor, is out in stable form after a September beta. The release adds UI refinements with more rounded corners, a new logo, fully 32-bit float audio processing, automatic audio ducking, and an update to FFmpeg 9.0.
keyPoints: UI improvements, more rounded corners, and a new logo
Audio pipeline now fully 32-bit float; optional automatic audio ducking
Updated against FFmpeg 9.0; binaries and source on GitHub
articles.whyItMatters: Shotcut users and Linux video editors get a refreshed interface and better audio handling in this release.

articles.title: GNOME 49.10 Released as the Final Update in the GNOME 49 Series
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: GNOME 49.10 is the final maintenance release for the GNOME 49 series, now end-of-life, updating 14 components with bug and stability fixes. GNOME 51 is the current stable generation and GNOME 50 the old-stable branch.
keyPoints: GNOME Shell fixes workspace glitches, Thunderbolt authorization, and lock-screen issues
Mutter fixes blurred rendering, rotated-display redraws, and multi-GPU scanout
GVfs fixes CVE-2026-88924; Epiphany patches autofill injection and path traversal flaws
articles.whyItMatters: Users on distributions still shipping GNOME 49 get a final round of fixes, including security patches, before support ends.

articles.title: Shotcut 26.9 Video Editor Adds Audio Ducking, FFmpeg 9.0
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: Shotcut 26.9 adds automatic audio ducking, per-track volume controls and meters in timeline headers, and Adjustment Clips that apply filters across all tracks beneath them. Audio now stays in 32-bit float internally, the multimedia framework moves to FFmpeg 9.0, and Linux gets VA-API HEVC, Vulkan, and SMB-share fixes.
keyPoints: Automatic audio ducking lowers music when dialogue tracks become active
Adjustment Clips apply filters to all video tracks underneath
Internal audio pipeline now 32-bit float; upgraded to FFmpeg 9.0
articles.whyItMatters: Video editors and podcast producers on Linux get mixing tools and hardware-encoding fixes without leaving a free, open-source editor.

articles.title: OpenShot 4.0.1 Video Editor Released with Timeline and Zoom Improvements
articles.brief: OpenShot 4.0.1, a bug-fix release of the open-source video editor, is available for download. It brings timeline and zoom improvements, an updated Razor tool, and faster keyframe and color editing.
articles.whyItMatters: OpenShot users get smoother timeline work and quicker editing tools in this update.

articles.title: Shotcut 26.9 Video Editor Improves VA-API HEVC Hardware Encoding on Linux
articles.brief: Shotcut 26.9 is out, improving the VA-API HEVC hardware encoder on Linux and adding Automatic Ducking for audio, volume control, and an audio level meter for timeline track headers.

articles.title: OpenShot 4.0.1 Video Editor Improves Razor Tool, Timeline Editing, and Linux Support
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: OpenShot 4.0.1 upgrades the Razor tool with source-frame previews, snapping, and ripple cuts, and improves timeline navigation and editing responsiveness. Linux users get official Snap support, native webcam discovery, and an optional Wayland capture module.
keyPoints: Razor tool gains frame previews, snapping, and automatic ripple cuts
Linux: official Snap support, webcam discovery, optional Wayland capture module
Fixes for undo history, exports, project saving, and macOS startup failures
articles.whyItMatters: Linux video editors and OpenShot users should care, as this update improves daily editing workflows and Linux integration.

articles.title: Silent Horizon gives Linux Mint a dramatic makeover — but at a CPU cost
articles.author: Joey Sneddon
articles.brief: Silent Horizon is a transformation script for Linux Mint's Cinnamon desktop that installs animated desklets, Plank dock themes and panel applets for a sleek, dark look. The animated weather and system monitor desklets look striking but drove Cinnamon CPU usage above 24% on low-powered hardware, causing slowdowns and…
keyPoints: Installs desklets, Plank dock theme, workspace switcher and tray applets via script
Weather desklet shows sun, moon and planet positions for your actual location
Animated desklets pushed Cinnamon CPU above 24%; removing them dropped it below 1%
articles.whyItMatters: Linux Mint users wanting a modern-looking desktop should know this pack delivers the visuals but may cripple weaker hardware.

articles.title: Linuxiac Weekly Wrap-Up: Week 39, 2026 (September 21–27)
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: Linuxiac's weekly roundup for September 21–27, 2026, covers a light week for distribution news but a long list of open-source software releases. Highlights include Systemd 262, COSMIC Desktop 1.9, GNOME 50.5, Samba 4.25, and Wireshark 4.6.9.
keyPoints: Systemd 262 adds static PID 1 builds plus better container, TPM, and VM support
COSMIC 1.9 adds a viewer and on-screen keyboard; GNOME 50.5 ships bug and security fixes
Wireshark 4.6.9 fixes 19 security vulnerabilities; Samba 4.25 adds clustering features
articles.whyItMatters: Linux users and admins wanting a quick scan of the week's FOSS releases and security fixes.

articles.title: Kernel prepatch 7.3-rc5 released
articles.author: corbet
articles.brief: Linus Torvalds released the fifth 7.3 release candidate, describing it as large but without an alarming pattern—just routine changes despite the sizable diffstat.
articles.whyItMatters: Kernel testers and developers tracking the 7.3 cycle should know this rc is large but considered normal.

articles.title: Linux 7.3-rc5 Released: "Another Week, Another Large RC"
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Linus Torvalds released Linux 7.3-rc5, an unusually large weekly test candidate, targeting a stable release around 18 October. Torvalds noted an odd diffstat with fewer driver patches and a quarter being selftests, but saw nothing alarming. Linux 7.3 will ship in Ubuntu 26.10 and other autumn distributions.
keyPoints: rc5 includes Cache Aware Scheduling fixes, new HID device support, and graphics driver fixes
Logitech Holt Receiver HID++ support reverted due to issues
AI/LLM agents credited with uncovering new issues in the ~41 million line codebase
articles.whyItMatters: Kernel testers and distro maintainers should test rc5 ahead of the mid-October Linux 7.3 stable release that will power Ubuntu 26.10.

articles.title: 9to5Linux Weekly Roundup: September 27th, 2026
articles.brief: This week's 9to5Linux roundup covers a long list of Linux software releases, including COSMIC 1.9, VLC 3.0.24, GNU Wget 2.3, Flatpak 1.18.3, GNOME 50.5, Firefox 156.0.1, OBS Studio 33 beta, and KeePassXC 2.8 beta.
articles.whyItMatters: Linux users who want a quick overview of the week's application and driver releases.

articles.title: Klassik Revives the KDE 3 Desktop on Modern Plasma 6
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: Klassik is a new open-source project recreating the KDE 3 desktop on top of the modern KDE Plasma 6 stack. Rather than just a theme, it rebuilds original KDE 3 components in Qt 6 and Qt Quick, with support for Wayland and fractional scaling.
keyPoints: Recreated KDE 3 panel applets include K Menu, Quicklaunch, task manager, and clocks, written in C++ and QML
The KDE 2/3 QStyle theme is rewritten for Qt 6; old KWin decorations are being ported to KDecoration3
Requires Qt 6, KDE Frameworks 6, and Plasma 6; install via CMake, use the latest tagged release
articles.whyItMatters: KDE users nostalgic for KDE 3 can get an authentic recreation on a fully modern, Wayland-capable Plasma 6 base.

articles.title: Budgie 10.10.3 Adds Favorites to Budgie Menu, Improves Labwc Bridge
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Budgie 10.10.3 is out, headlined by a Favorites area in the Budgie Menu so apps can finally be pinned there. The point release also improves the Labwc bridge for the recommended Wayland compositor and adds primary monitor designation, freely placed desktop icons, and oo7 Secret Service support.
keyPoints: Budgie Menu gains a Favorites area for pinning applications
Labwc bridge gets keybinding, multimedia key, and reliability fixes
Adds primary monitor selection and oo7 Secret Service support
articles.whyItMatters: Budgie desktop users, especially those on Wayland with Labwc, get long-requested menu favorites and smoother compositor integration.

articles.title: Budgie 10.10.3 Desktop Environment Introduces Free Placement of Desktop Icons
articles.brief: Budgie 10.10.3 is out as the third maintenance update to the Wayland-only Budgie 10.10 series, adding free placement of desktop icons among various improvements and bug fixes.
articles.whyItMatters: Budgie users tracking the Wayland-only 10.10 series will want to know about this maintenance update and its desktop icon feature.

articles.title: Budgie Desktop 10.10.3 Released With Menu Favorites, Free Desktop Icon Placement
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: Budgie 10.10.3, the third maintenance update in the 10.10 series, adds favorites to Budgie Menu, restores the Wayland-compatible Keyboard Layout applet, and lets users place desktop icons freely instead of on a fixed grid.
keyPoints: Right-click apps to add them to a new Favorites category in Budgie Menu
Desktop icons can now be placed freely, with auto-arrange, snap-to-grid, and multi-select
Keyboard Layout applet rewritten in C to work under Wayland
articles.whyItMatters: Budgie users, especially on Wayland or multi-monitor setups, get long-requested usability fixes and features; packagers can note the optional oo7 Secret Service support.

articles.title: postmarketOS Rebrands as Nura After 18-Month Naming Process
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: Mobile Linux project postmarketOS has renamed itself Nura, announced at its conference. The name comes from Sardinia's ancient Nuraghe stone structures, symbolizing longevity. The old name was hard to trademark, often miscapitalized, and no longer fit a project now shipping preinstalled on PinePhones.
keyPoints: Nura is short for Nuraghe, ancient Sardinian stone towers built to last
Old name was untrademarkable; Nura trademark application filed
Over 300 community names submitted; Nura won an internal team vote
articles.whyItMatters: Users and contributors of the mobile Linux distro should know the project, packages, and documentation will gradually move to the Nura name and nura.eco domain.

articles.title: Noctalia 5.2 Wayland Shell Released With Redesigned Window Switcher
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: Noctalia 5.2, a desktop shell for Wayland, arrives with an animated window-switcher carousel, calendar reminders from iCalendar, CalDAV, and Google Calendar, plus Freedesktop sound theme support.
keyPoints: Redesigned window switcher with animated preview carousel and workspace filtering
Calendar reminders for iCalendar, CalDAV, and Google Calendar with configurable lead times
Sound theme support, annotation editor for existing images, Japanese localization
articles.whyItMatters: Wayland users running Noctalia or considering alternative desktop shells gain workflow improvements and broad bug fixes worth reviewing.

articles.title: Linux Kernel's LZ4 Compression Code Being Resynced for Better Performance
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Samsung's Michal Wilczynski posted patches to overhaul the kernel's LZ4 code, which has been a stale fork of upstream since 2017-2018. The changes vendor upstream LZ4 unmodified, bringing bug fixes and up to 21% higher in-kernel benchmark performance.
keyPoints: In-kernel LZ4 fork last synced with upstream around 2017-2018
Patches let upstream LZ4 code be copied into kernel tree unmodified
EROFS sees ~11-14% higher read throughput; other benchmarks up to 21% faster
articles.whyItMatters: Kernel developers and users of LZ4-compressed filesystems like EROFS gain performance and easier future updates.

articles.title: Apprise 2.0 Notification Tool Released With Smarter Retries and Async Support
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: Apprise 2.0 launches the notification framework's new major series with a rebuilt architecture, adding template variables, tag escalation, selective retries, parallel delivery, timeouts, and native async support. It is a breaking release for 1.x API users; a supported apprise-v1-release branch remains available.
keyPoints: Retries now track per-recipient results and resend only to failed destinations
New AppriseResult object gives detailed per-service statuses and logs from notify()
Adds Delta Chat, WPUSH, YouLMK, and Telnyx SMS services; breaking change for 1.x API
articles.whyItMatters: Developers and sysadmins using Apprise for multi-service notifications should review the breaking API changes before upgrading.

articles.title: Intel lands big memory hotplugging speedup for Linux 7.4
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Intel's Yuan Liu has queued patches into mm/core.git's for-next branch that optimize zone contiguous checks to speed up memory hotplugging, expected for the Linux 7.4 merge window. Testing shows up to an 81% time reduction for VM memory hotplugging and up to 75% for unplugging, with Samsung also seeing large CXL…
keyPoints: Avoids page block by page block scans across entire zones during hotplug
Up to 81% faster VM memory hotplug, 75% faster unplug
Expected in Linux 7.4 via mm/core.git for-next branch
articles.whyItMatters: Operators of virtual machines and CXL-based memory expansion systems will see much faster memory hot add/remove operations.

articles.title: Linux Patches Enable ThinkPad X1 Carbon G14's IR Camera
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: New kernel patches from Ruslan Koreev enable the second MIPI IR camera on Lenovo's Panther Lake-based ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen 14, which is used for Windows Hello-style face authentication. The main RGB camera already works on Linux. The patches are under review and may land in Linux v7.4.
keyPoints: Sensor is an ST VD55G1 monochrome global-shutter unit, powered via an INT3472 device.
Patches add ACPI wiring and monochrome pixel formats to the Intel IPU7 ISYS.
Tested on Fedora 44: streams via libcamera and works with howdy face authentication.
articles.whyItMatters: Owners or prospective buyers of the ThinkPad X1 Carbon Gen 14 on Linux gain IR face-authentication support if these patches are merged.

articles.title: New Patch Series Working Toward DRBD 9 Support In The Linux Kernel
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: LINBIT developers sent a new patch series to the LKML preparing to bring DRBD 9 support into the mainline Linux kernel. The prep patches restructure the in-kernel DRBD 8.4 code to match the out-of-tree layout and raise limits to DRBD 9 values, with the full DRBD 9 patches hoped to follow.
keyPoints: Patches restructure in-kernel DRBD 8.4 code to align with LINBIT's out-of-tree driver
Series raises various limits to match DRBD 9 values
DRBD 9 adds 32-node replication, load balancing, quorum management, faster I/O
articles.whyItMatters: Cluster and storage administrators relying on out-of-tree DRBD builds should care, since mainline DRBD 9 would simplify deployment and maintenance of replicated block storage.

articles.title: AlmaLinux Opens Free, Community-Driven Software and Hardware Certification
articles.author: Sourav Rudra
articles.brief: AlmaLinux now offers free software certification: publishers list products and users confirm they work on their own hardware. The alma-certify hardware tool was rewritten for sub-10-minute runs, works from live media without installation, and all results land in a public, searchable catalog.
keyPoints: Software certification is free; users confirm compatibility via an account on the portal
alma-certify rewritten: sub-10-minute runs, live-media support, QR-code registration
Results go to a public catalog with a free read-only API, tracked per major release
articles.whyItMatters: AlmaLinux users and admins can verify hardware and software compatibility before deploying, and submissions push vendors toward official support.

articles.title: Improved GPU Reset Coming For Raspberry Pi Boards With Linux 7.4
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: A DRM-Misc-Next pull request adds improved GPU reset support for the Broadcom V3D GPU in the VC4 kernel driver. Igalia's Maíra Canal switched the driver to use the V3D reset controller, replacing a cumbersome private refcount workaround. The code targets the Linux 7.4 merge window in October.
keyPoints: VC4 driver now uses the BCM2835 PM block's V3D reset line instead of forcing PM counts to zero
GPU can be reset without power-cycling its domain, improving hang recovery
Reset line is optional; device trees without it keep driver-side recovery
articles.whyItMatters: Raspberry Pi and Broadcom-based hardware users should see more reliable recovery from GPU hangs.

articles.title: Replacing the old battery on rechargeable bike lights
articles.brief: Julia Evans revived ten-year-old rechargeable bike lights by replacing their dead batteries. With minimal electronics experience, she cut open the silicone casing, desoldered the old cells, identified them as LIR2477 coin cells, and soldered in replacements ordered from AliExpress for about $20 CAD in parts.
keyPoints: Identified the mystery battery as an LIR2477 by asking an LLM
Used a desoldering pump and iFixit guide for a first-ever desoldering job
Repair cost about $20 CAD; both lights work again
articles.whyItMatters: Encouraging read for anyone curious about repairing old electronics without prior soldering experience.

articles.title: Solus Linux Adopts Formal AI and LLM Contribution Policy
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: Solus Linux has published a policy governing AI and LLM use in contributions. AI-assisted code is allowed if developers test it, take responsibility, and mark commits with an 'Assisted-by LLM' note, but AI-generated content is banned from blogs and official communications.
keyPoints: AI-assisted contributions allowed; submitters must test and take full responsibility
Commits using AI must carry an 'Assisted-by LLM' note; no bot submissions
No AI-generated material in Solus blog or official communications
articles.whyItMatters: Solus contributors and packagers need to know the disclosure rules to avoid having work rejected or being blocked.

articles.title: Incus 7.5 Adds OVN Child Networks, Live Instance Moves
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: Incus 7.5 lands with OVN child networks, live migration of instances across projects and cluster members, and improvements to storage, authorization, monitoring, and VM support. It also fixes 11 security vulnerabilities, several critical, including arbitrary host file writes via migration and Btrfs backup paths.
keyPoints: OVN child networks share a parent router, uplink, and peerings while keeping own subnets
Instances can move projects while live-migrating to another cluster member
11 vulnerabilities fixed, including critical host file write and auth bypass flaws
articles.whyItMatters: Incus administrators should upgrade promptly given the critical security fixes, and cluster operators gain useful networking and migration features.

articles.title: GNOME OS Developers Unveil Toolpak, a Flatpak-Like System for Developer Tools
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: GNOME developer Jordan Petridis introduced Toolpak, a packaging concept from GNOME OS developers aimed at developer tools that don't fit Flatpak's sandboxing model. It uses UAPL3 discoverable disk images, mount namespaces, and unrestricted system access, with a prototype in progress.
keyPoints: Flatpak's confinement doesn't suit tools like QEMU and strace; Toolpak fills that gap
Uses UAPL3 disk images, mount namespaces, and $PATH prepending with full system access
Aims for reproducible builds, SBOM/licensing compliance; apps fit for Flatpak are rejected
articles.whyItMatters: Developers on GNOME OS who need containerized tools without sandboxing restrictions should watch this prototype.

articles.title: MM Change Slated For Linux 7.4 Yields +22904539.81% In One Metric
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: A memory management patch queued for Linux 7.4 lets sheaf refills draw from the barn first, fixing saturation that forced RCU sheaf flushes. The 81-line change improves a will-it-scale mmap1 test by 24% and shows extreme gains in barn_get/barn_put metrics.
keyPoints: Sheaf refills now take objects from the barn first, using a new partial sheaf for leftovers
Benchmarks show 24% mmap1 improvement and huge barn_get/barn_put gains
81 lines of new code, queued for the Linux 7.4 merge window in late October
articles.whyItMatters: Kernel developers and performance-focused admins should track allocator changes that may improve memory-heavy workloads in Linux 7.4.

articles.title: GDB 18.1 released with Windows improvements, new commands, and Python API additions
articles.author: corbet
articles.brief: Version 18.1 of the GNU Debugger is out. Highlights include major Windows native target improvements such as non-stop mode and true-color support, new commands for saving history and managing subprocess environments, two new targets, and a long list of Python API and remote protocol additions, alongside several…
keyPoints: Windows target gains non-stop mode, scheduler-locking, TLS support, and true-color console output
New commands save history, skips, and user commands; new MicroBlaze Linux and AArch64 MinGW targets
Removes stabs, mdebug, CTF trace support, old .gdb_index versions, and AIX 7.1 support
articles.whyItMatters: Developers who debug with GDB, especially on Windows or via its Python API, should review the incompatible changes before upgrading.

articles.title: virtio-nvgpu Brings Shared NVIDIA GPU Access to Linux KVM Guests
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: Nestri Labs is building virtio-nvgpu, an experimental virtio device that lets multiple Linux KVM guests share a single NVIDIA GPU without PCI passthrough. It works at the NVIDIA kernel-driver ABI level, claims about 2% overhead versus bare metal, and was demoed with four guests on one RTX 3060.
keyPoints: GPU stays on host; multiple guests share it via a custom virtio device
Demoed four guests on one GeForce RTX 3060 simultaneously
Supports Vulkan, Wayland, NVENC, basic CUDA enumeration
articles.whyItMatters: Developers and homelabbers wanting shared NVIDIA GPUs for game streaming or virtualized desktops should watch this, as it removes the one-GPU-per-VM passthrough constraint.

articles.title: OBS Studio 33 Nears Release: Here's What to Expect
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: OBS Studio 33 is approaching stable release, now at Beta 4. Headline changes include a Chromium Embedded Framework upgrade, a reworked plugin loading system, improved source snapping, and numerous usability and platform-specific fixes, including dropping Ubuntu 24.04 support.
keyPoints: CEF browser backend updated from July 2024 to September 2026 codebase
Plugin loading overhauled; old third-party locations work only until OBS 34
Source snapping improved with visual indicator and axis-wide snapping
articles.whyItMatters: Streamers and OBS plugin developers should review the plugin path changes and test browser sources before the stable release.

articles.title: GNOME 50.5 Improves Multi-Monitor Support, HDR Support, and More
articles.brief: GNOME 50.5 is out as the fifth update to the GNOME 50 desktop series, bringing bug fixes, updated translations, and improvements to multi-monitor and HDR support.
articles.whyItMatters: GNOME users on multi-monitor or HDR setups may want to update for these fixes.

articles.title: Fastfetch 2.69 Adds Animated Logos, Better Linux and Bluetooth Support
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: Fastfetch 2.69, the command-line system information tool, adds animated GIF and APNG logo support via the Kitty graphics protocol, plus a logo.position auto mode for narrow terminals. It drops the ImageMagick dependency on Windows, macOS, and Android, and expands Linux detection for CRUX, SPARC CPUs, and COSMIC.
keyPoints: Animated GIF/APNG logos via Kitty protocol, with fallback to built-in logo
Native image libraries replace ImageMagick on Windows, macOS, Android
Bluetooth LE detection, Core versions up to 6.3, signal quality reporting
articles.whyItMatters: Users and package maintainers of the popular system info tool get richer logo display and fewer dependencies.

articles.title: Linux 7.3-rc5 DRM fixes: Nouveau suspend/resume, Intel Xe power brake, AI-found bugs
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: A heavy batch of DRM subsystem fixes landed ahead of Linux 7.3-rc5, many of them AI-inspired fixes for error paths, leaks, and use-after-frees. Nouveau got the most fixes, including a suspend/resume regression from the move to NVIDIA R570 firmware, while Intel's Xe driver gained a new "power brake" throttle reason for…
keyPoints: Many fixes for error handling, leaks, and use-after-frees were found via AI/LLMs
Nouveau fixed suspend/resume regressions and vRAM pinning with R570 firmware
Intel Xe now reports PWRBRK power brake throttling for Crescent Island accelerators
articles.whyItMatters: Kernel graphics users, especially NVIDIA-on-Nouveau users hit by suspend/resume bugs, should track these fixes in Linux 7.3.

articles.title: Wisp GNOME Shell Extension Simplifies Btrfs Snapshot Management
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Wisp is a new GNOME Shell extension that provides a graphical interface to Snapper for managing Btrfs file-system snapshots, highlighted in the latest This Week in GNOME. It lets users view changed files between snapshots, adjust retention policies, and create snapshots manually.
keyPoints: Wisp wraps Snapper with a GUI for Btrfs snapshots on GNOME
Shows file changes between snapshots and adjusts retention policies
Available from extensions.gnome.org and GitHub
articles.whyItMatters: GNOME users on Btrfs systems who prefer not to use Snapper from the command line gain a graphical management option.

articles.title: AMDXDNA Linux driver gains NPU3 kernel-mode command submission patches
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: AMD engineer David Zhang has posted 21 patches extending the open-source AMDXDNA kernel driver for NPU3 (AIE4) hardware found in Ryzen AI 300 series SoCs. The series adds kernel-mode command submission, device telemetry queries, and full system and runtime power management including suspend/resume.
keyPoints: 21 patches on LKML target AIE4/NPU3 hardware in Ryzen AI 300 SoCs
Kernel-mode command submission replaces userspace doorbell mapping as default path
Adds suspend/resume and runtime PM across PF, VF, and Classic devices with SR-IOV linking
articles.whyItMatters: Developers and users of Ryzen AI 300 laptops should care, as this work improves upstream Linux support and power behavior for their NPU hardware.

articles.title: KDE Plasma 6.8 Continues With Last Minute Tweaks & Fixes
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Alongside Plasma 6.8 Beta 2 and the Akademy conference, KDE developers landed last-minute UI refinements, a crash fix, and a Bluetooth wizard improvement for Plasma 6.8. Early Plasma 6.9 work includes better currency conversion handling in KRunner searches.
keyPoints: Improved click feedback for system tray icons in Plasma 6.8
Fixes crash when deleting starred clipboard entry from Meta+V pop-up
Bluetooth wizard can find BLE devices while other apps hold a discovery session
articles.whyItMatters: KDE Plasma users and testers tracking the 6.8 release should know what late fixes to expect in the final build.

articles.title: PeaZip 11.3 File Archiver Adds Safer PEA Extraction
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: PeaZip 11.3 tightens security: a master password is now mandatory for the password manager, sensitive file types require confirmation before opening, and PEA archives extract to a temporary directory until validated. The release also fixes ZPAQ crashes, adds an 'Open with' screen, and updates 7z/p7zip and PEA backends.
keyPoints: Master password now mandatory; export stored passwords before upgrading
PEA extraction validated in temp directory before moving to output
New Shift+F12 'Open with' screen, themes, and 7z 26.03 / PEA 1.33 backends
articles.whyItMatters: PeaZip users get safer archive extraction and file launching, and should export saved passwords before upgrading.

articles.title: PeaZip 11.3 Archive Manager Improves ZPAQ Support, Adds New Themes
articles.brief: PeaZip 11.3, the open-source archive manager, is now available with improved ZPAQ support, new themes, a new keyboard shortcut, and better handling of invalid filenames.
articles.whyItMatters: PeaZip users get improved ZPAQ archive handling and a refreshed look.

articles.title: Era, a Rust-based calendar app for GNOME, enters beta on Flathub
articles.author: Joey Sneddon
articles.brief: Era is a new GTK4/libadwaita calendar app for GNOME written in Rust, now available in beta on Flathub. It offers year, month and agenda views, event editing, .ics import and online sync, routing Evolution Data Server calls through a swappable middle layer called Clepsydre.
keyPoints: Beta installable from Flathub; clean, adaptive GTK4/libadwaita UI
Uses Evolution Data Server indirectly via hot-swappable Clepsydre layer
Supports local use, .ics import and sync with online providers
articles.whyItMatters: GNOME users looking for a modern alternative to GNOME Calendar can test it now.

articles.title: OBS Studio 33 beta adds latest NVIDIA Broadcast SDK support
articles.brief: OBS Studio 33 entered public beta with support for the newest NVIDIA Broadcast SDKs for audio and video effects. It also adds a check for missing encoders when loading a profile.
articles.whyItMatters: Streamers and content creators using OBS with NVIDIA GPUs can test the beta for updated effects support.

articles.title: New FUTEX syscalls back in development to aid Valve's ARM64 gaming efforts
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Igalia has posted an updated version of its get_robust_list2 and set_robust_list2 FUTEX syscall patches, designed to improve FEX-Emu and other emulation layers running x86 games on ARM64, including Valve's Steam Frame. The rebase against mainline was delayed while a race condition was fixed.
keyPoints: Patches target shortcomings of existing robust list syscalls for emulation layers like FEX-Emu
First update since late November; rebased on mainline with VDSO adaptations
Work supports Steam Play gaming on ARM64 devices such as Steam Frame
articles.whyItMatters: Developers working on Linux gaming, ARM64 emulation, or kernel FUTEX code should track these patches as they underpin Valve's ARM64 gaming strategy.

articles.title: Shelly 3.1.5 Arch Linux Package Manager Expands AUR Support
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: Shelly 3.1.5, a graphical Arch package manager covering repos, AUR, Flatpaks, and AppImages, adds an optional atoll-powered AUR browser with sorting and search. It also introduces a `shelly build --install` workflow, a `repo-db` command for pacman-compatible databases, and numerous build, search, and error-handling…
keyPoints: Optional atoll-based AUR browser with pagination, sorting, and multiple search modes
New `shelly build --install` and `shelly repo-db` command families
Fixes for repository search, AUR `--needed` support, and corrupt config recovery
articles.whyItMatters: Arch Linux users who manage packages graphically gain broader AUR tooling and more reliable builds in a single app.

articles.title: Nginx Proxy Manager 2.16 Adds Built-In Log Viewer
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: Nginx Proxy Manager 2.16 adds a web-based log viewer and per-path access lists for proxy hosts. Security changes include token invalidation after password changes, local 2FA QR generation, and removal of DNS credentials after Certbot runs. A Certbot update may break some DNS plugins.
keyPoints: New integrated log viewer and per-path access lists in the web UI
Security fixes: token invalidation, local 2FA QR codes, DNS credential cleanup
Certbot update may break existing DNS plugins; check setups after upgrading
articles.whyItMatters: Self-hosters using Nginx Proxy Manager for reverse proxying and TLS should review the release, especially if they rely on DNS-based certificate validation.

articles.title: Shelly 3.1.5 GUI Package Manager for Arch Linux Adds Atoll-Powered AUR Browser
articles.brief: Shelly 3.1.5, a graphical package manager for Arch Linux, is now available. It adds an Atoll-powered AUR browser, a build-and-install command, and native tools for maintaining your own package repositories.
articles.whyItMatters: Arch Linux users who prefer GUI tools for AUR packages and personal repositories may find this update useful.

articles.title: GDB 18.1 Debugger Brings Better Windows Support
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: GDB 18.1 is out with major Windows improvements: native TLS variable support, non-stop mode on Windows 10 and later, scheduler locking, better Windows Terminal console support, and consistent forward-slash filenames.
keyPoints: Windows gains native TLS variables, non-stop mode, and scheduler locking
Adds AArch64 MinGW target and FPMR support on AArch64
New commands: "save history", "set/show/unset local-environment", "info proc environ"
articles.whyItMatters: Developers who debug C/C++, Rust, or other languages on Windows get a substantially improved GNU Debugger experience.

articles.title: How KDE got funding to add enterprise features
articles.author: jzb
articles.brief: The Sovereign Tech Agency is investing nearly €1.3 million in KDE through 2027. At Akademy 2026, Nate Graham and Kevin Ottens explained how the funding was secured and offered tips for other projects seeking similar support.

articles.title: Banshee music player returns as a Snap package
articles.author: Joey Sneddon
articles.brief: Alan Pope packaged Banshee 2.6.2, the final 2014 stable release, as a Snap with compatibility fixes and some restored online services. It works as a functional music player on modern desktops, though some features like Last.fm login and video playback fail, and its GTK2 UI scales poorly on modern displays.
keyPoints: Snap bundles old dependencies via Core22 without affecting the host system
Music playback, album art, MPRIS, and media keys all work
Last.fm auth and video playback broken; GTK2 UI struggles with fractional scaling
articles.whyItMatters: Nostalgic Linux users and software preservation fans can run a classic app that distros dropped years ago.

articles.title: Redox OS Adds IO_uring-Like API, NUMA Support, and Working QEMU
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Redox OS's August status update covers an IO_uring-like ring buffer API, initial NUMA support, and QEMU now running on the OS, though without hardware acceleration. The update also brings dual boot support from Linux, initial multi-core support on ARM64, about 5% lower IPC overhead, and a smaller kernel binary.
keyPoints: Ring buffer API akin to Linux's IO_uring, targeting better NVMe I/O performance
QEMU runs on Redox but lacks KVM-like acceleration, so it is very slow
Initial NUMA support, ARM64 multi-core support, and dual boot from Linux
articles.whyItMatters: Developers following alternative operating systems can see how Redox, the Rust-based OS, is closing feature gaps with Linux.

articles.title: Jeff Geerling announces HomelabFest, St. Louis, September 2027
articles.author: jeff@jeffgeerling.com (Jeff Geerling)
articles.brief: Jeff Geerling is launching HomelabFest, a conference for the homelab community, set for September 12-14, 2027 in St. Louis (technically St. Charles). He is inviting content creators, self-hosting companies, and attendees, with 250 'Super Early Bird' tickets at $100.
keyPoints: Event runs September 12-14, 2027 in St. Charles, near St. Louis
Focus areas include networking, mini racks, servers, 3D printing, self-hosted software
250 Super Early Bird tickets at $100; community tables offered near cost
articles.whyItMatters: Homelab enthusiasts and self-hosting fans get a first dedicated in-person gathering organized by a prominent community figure.

articles.title: Linux 7.2.8 and 6.18.54 stable kernels released
articles.author: jzb
articles.brief: Greg Kroah-Hartman announced the 7.2.8 and 6.18.54 stable kernel releases. Both contain important fixes throughout the tree, and users are advised to upgrade.
articles.whyItMatters: Administrators and users tracking stable kernels should plan to update.

articles.title: A summary from the 2026 Git Contributors' Summit
articles.author: corbet
articles.brief: Johannes Schindelin has posted a detailed summary of the 2026 Git Contributors' Summit discussions. Topics include Git 3.0, the security process, documentation, the pluggable object database, and use of LLMs.
articles.whyItMatters: Git contributors and users interested in the project's direction will find the summit outcomes relevant.

articles.title: Phoronix: Linux kernel builds approach the 10-second mark
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Phoronix reports that defconfig x86_64 kernel builds now take about 15-20 seconds on high-end dual EPYC hardware, with 10 seconds in sight. Lorenzo Stoakes' AI-assisted kbuild patch series, now at v4, cuts build times ~36% (and incremental builds ~70%) by removing parallelism bottlenecks, and may land in Linux 7.4.
keyPoints: Stoakes' kbuild patches make kernel builds ~36% faster, incremental builds ~70% faster
Dual EPYC 9754 server defconfig build dropped from 28 to 20 seconds
allmodconfig builds now drop under two minutes
articles.whyItMatters: Kernel developers and anyone bisecting or building kernels benefit from dramatically faster clean and incremental builds, even on non-flagship hardware.

articles.title: Security updates for Friday
articles.author: jzb
articles.brief: LWN's roundup of security updates published September 24-25, 2026, covering AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora, Mageia, Oracle, Slackware, SUSE, and Ubuntu. Notable updates include kernel fixes across several distributions, plus curl, expat, openssl, unbound, squid, and webkitgtk patches.
keyPoints: Kernel updates for AlmaLinux 8, SUSE, and multiple Ubuntu releases
Ubuntu patched curl, expat, gdal, libpcap, and kernel packages across many LTS releases
SUSE and openSUSE issued a large batch including chromium, libsoup, libx11, and rabbitmq-server
articles.whyItMatters: System administrators should scan this list for packages running on their systems and apply relevant patches.

articles.title: systemd Gets Built-In System Reporting With systemd-report
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: systemd is gaining a reporting subsystem called systemd-report that collects static system facts and dynamic runtime metrics into a single timestamped, optionally signed JSON report. Reports can be uploaded to a central HTTPS server on a timer or on boot, reboot, and shutdown events, targeting fleet management.
keyPoints: Gathers system facts and runtime metrics via a generic Varlink interface into one JSON report
Supports three signing methods: local software key, TPM quote, or CPU TSM quote
Periodic or event-triggered HTTPS PUT uploads for remote fleet management
articles.whyItMatters: Admins managing large Linux fleets get a signed, snapshot-based reporting framework built into systemd instead of separate monitoring agents.

articles.title: Dutch Government Builds NixOS-Based Desktop After Microsoft Cut Off the ICC
articles.author: Sourav Rudra
articles.brief: After US sanctions cut the ICC prosecutor off from Microsoft services, the Dutch government launched DAWO, a sovereign digital work environment built on NixOS. The framework covers OS, office suite, collaboration, cloud, and AI, with eight municipalities running pilots and a stable release planned for next year.
keyPoints: DAWO is a full sovereign stack covering OS, office suite, cloud, and AI
NixOS chosen as a Dutch project; openSUSE and Fedora rejected over US commercial ties
Pilots run on decommissioned laptops; 80-90% of configuration carries between deployments
articles.whyItMatters: Linux users and open-source advocates should care: a national government is standardizing on NixOS specifically to escape US vendor dependency.

articles.title: Patches Posted For Enabling NVMe On All Apple M3 SoCs With Linux
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Janne Grunau posted a seven-patch series enabling NVMe storage on all Apple M3, M3 Pro, Max, and Ultra devices under Linux. The NVMe works as on M2 Pro/Max/Ultra, but needs ~140 lines of Device Tree and YAML additions. The patches may land in the Linux 7.4 merge window.
keyPoints: Seven-patch series enables NVMe across all Apple M3 variants
Requires ~140 lines of Device Tree and YAML additions
May make the Linux 7.4 merge window; M3 users should use Asahi Linux meanwhile
articles.whyItMatters: Developers and users running Linux on Apple M3 hardware need mainline NVMe support for usable storage.

articles.title: AMD Linux patches improve HDMI 2.1 reliability ahead of Linux 7.4
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: AMD sent out new AMDGPU Display Core patches fixing HDMI 2.1 reliability issues, such as skipping FRL status polling when the link is down and aligning LT timeout with the HDMI spec. This comes ahead of Linux 7.4, where HDMI 2.1 will be enabled by default with FreeSync, VRR, and ALLM.
keyPoints: Fix skips HDMI FRL status polling when link is down, avoiding blank displays on hot-plug
HDMI 2.1 LT timeout fix aligns with spec; FRL polling serialized against link detect
Patches also advance DCN 4.2 and DCN 6.0 support; DCN 6 likely tied to next-gen RDNA5 GPUs
articles.whyItMatters: AMD GPU users on Linux with HDMI 2.1 displays should care, as these fixes reduce display failures ahead of default HDMI 2.1 support in Linux 7.4.

articles.title: Last call for Phoronix Premium autumn sale: $35/year or $160 lifetime
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Phoronix's autumn Premium sale ends Sunday, 27 September, offering ad-free subscriptions at $35/year (normally $45) or $160 lifetime (normally $250). The site says Premium revenue funds its Linux hardware reviews and benchmarks, noting that under 1% of readers subscribe while most ads are blocked.
keyPoints: Sale ends end of day Sunday, 27 September, any timezone
$35/year instead of $45; $160 lifetime instead of $250
Premium includes ad-free reading, single-page articles, dark mode, priority feedback
articles.whyItMatters: Regular Phoronix readers who want to support independent Linux hardware coverage can get the discounted rate this weekend.

articles.title: Go's expanding SIMD support adds platform-independent interface
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: A new Go.dev blog post details Go's experimental SIMD support, introduced in Go 1.26 for x86_64 AVX and expanded in Go 1.27 to ARM64 NEON plus a portable, platform- and size-agnostic interface modeled on Google's Highway library. Go 1.28 plans to add Arm SVE support and more SIMD operations.
keyPoints: Go 1.26 added experimental SIMD APIs targeting x86_64 AVX
SIMD package covers AVX, AVX2, AVX-512, ARM NEON, and WASM SIMD
Go 1.27 added a portable, platform-agnostic SIMD interface inspired by Google Highway
articles.whyItMatters: Go developers writing performance-critical code can use vectorized CPU instructions without architecture-specific code.

articles.title: Samba 4.25 Released With Experimental SMB3 Persistent Handles
articles.author: Michael Larabel
articles.brief: Samba 4.25 is out, adding experimental SMB3 Persistent Handles so clients can reconnect after a server restart while keeping their file handles, though at a significant performance cost. It also adds a Ceph RGW VFS module, improved JSON audit logging, and AES as the default domain encryption type.
keyPoints: Experimental SMB3 Persistent Handles enable uninterrupted file access after server restarts
Persistent handles carry a significant performance cost from double storage per operation
New Ceph RGW VFS module exports Ceph Object Gateway buckets as SMB shares
articles.whyItMatters: Admins running Samba file services gain failover resilience and new Ceph integration, but must weigh the performance trade-off of persistent handles.

articles.title: Mageia 9 support ends September 30, users urged to upgrade to Mageia 10
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: Mageia 9, released in August 2023, reaches end of support on September 30, 2026 and will stop receiving security fixes. Users can upgrade via the system tray update tool or command line, or do a clean install of Mageia 10.
keyPoints: Support ends September 30, 2026, three months after Mageia 10's June 30 release
Upgrade via system tray app, command line, or clean install; Live images cannot upgrade
Mageia 10 ships kernel 6.18 LTS, Plasma 6.5, GNOME 49, DNF 5
articles.whyItMatters: Mageia 9 users must upgrade before September 30 to keep receiving security updates.

articles.title: Samba 4.25 Released With New High-Availability and Clustering Features
articles.author: Bobby Borisov
articles.brief: Samba 4.25 is out as the first stable release in the new series. Its headline addition is experimental SMB3 Persistent Handles for high-availability setups, plus a new Ceph RGW VFS module, safer cluster rolling upgrades, and stronger Kerberos encryption defaults.
keyPoints: Experimental SMB3 Persistent Handles let clients keep open files across server restarts
New vfs_ceph_rgw module exposes Ceph Object Gateway buckets as SMB shares
